questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The ability to study viticulture and oenology.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses have been a difficult to follow, but overall a really really good experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The study coordinator from the University of Milan was extremely helpful and provided much-needed information. In general, the Italian systems are very different to the Danish and I used a lot of time sending e-mails, finding courses, asking for permission to follow them, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I only got assistance from the study coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was no assistance or orientation provided by the host institution, as I picked my courses by interest and didn't study a program. As is my own choice I am very satisfied with it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It is tough to find an affordable place to live in Milan, but it's not impossible. 
I hit the jackpot and found an apartment in a central location with cheap rent. 
My experience is to search in groups on Facebook and not expect it to be cheaper than the rent in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
The interior style of a furnished apartment is very Italian. 
For me, living off campus was the right thing, as there are a lot of classes on campus so it was nice to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy and helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The process took a long time, as the course catalogue wasn't updated when I had to register for courses, so I wrote to many professors asking for information about the courses. 
Some of the courses were not available or changed the scheme location, so I, unfortunately, could not follow all of my first choices as planned. 
After finding available courses, I had to ask each professor for permission to follow the course before choosing them for my OLA.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The study coordinator was a really really big help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful as I only got 2 out of 6 courses that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose a programme to follow, as I ended up with scheme overlaps and a lot of courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was all graduate and some of them were at a really high level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The teaching style is very Italian, and there were a few professors who had such a strong Italian accent, that they were impossible to understand.
Almost all classes are held as a lecture by a professor sitting down and reading up from their own slides, not providing any books or supplementary literature. 
Very few classes have group work or any type of discussion during class. 
Furthermore, no lab was provided in chemical courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fermentation biotechnology
Molecular and cellular microbiology
Agricultural systems and soil science
Molecular bases of taste 
Food product design and development
Italian Language SLAM

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Agricultural systems and soil science and Molecular bases of taste. 
The professors were welcoming and their syllabus was very interesting. 
Also, the Italian Language course was really good and taught me a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus network is really strong in Milan and offers a lot of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus network.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Venice and the Como lakes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, as a lot of locals speak English and are really welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just speak to them - they are all really friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of cultural differences, both socially and at uni. 
At the university, the students are a lot younger than at UPCH and the interaction between students/professors is very formal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The social part of the culture - everybody is welcoming and encouraging.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Find outside-campus housing. 
2) Choose courses that are used to having exchange students. 
3)  Seek out the local students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Learn as much Italian as possible before going.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to study at an Italian University and living in Italy for six months.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The Italian language and being okay with the Italian way of living - also at the university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I cannot recommend it more, it has overall been an amazing experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
